title: One LNS step on an inspection week

blocks.text: A utility's inspection planner picks which substation inspections the crews run this week. Each job has a district, a value (risk points removed) and the crew-hours it takes; the crews have `hours` in total. `build(jobs, hours)` in `inspections.py` already makes the whole week's CP-SAT model, with one Boolean `pick[name]` per job.
The planner has a plan and wants to improve it one district at a time: free the jobs of one district, keep every other job exactly as the plan has it, and let CP-SAT re-plan the freed part.
Write `improve(jobs, hours, plan, free)`. `plan` and `free` are sets of job names. Return the set of job names in the best plan that agrees with `plan` on every job not in `free`.
The model `build` makes, with $`J`$ the jobs, $`v_j`$ their values and $`h_j`$ their hours:

Write the rows your step adds in this notation first, with their quantifier: one for the jobs the plan runs and one for the jobs it leaves out, each only outside the neighborhood. Then code them, hint the current plan, and solve with one worker. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Job:
    name: str
    district: str
    value: int      # risk removed, in points
    hours: int      # crew-hours the inspection takes


def build(jobs: list[Job], hours: int) -> tuple[cp_model.CpModel, dict[str, cp_model.IntVar]]:
    """Given: the week's model. pick[j] = 1 runs job j; the crews have `hours` in total."""
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    pick = {j.name: model.new_bool_var(f"pick_{j.name}") for j in jobs}
    model.add(sum(j.hours * pick[j.name] for j in jobs) <= hours)
    model.maximize(sum(j.value * pick[j.name] for j in jobs))
    return model, pick


def improve(jobs: list[Job], hours: int, plan: set[str], free: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    """The best plan that keeps every job outside `free` exactly as `plan` has it."""
    model, pick = build(jobs, hours)
    for name, var in pick.items():
        model.add_hint(var, 1 if name in plan else 0)
        if name not in free:
            model.add(var == (1 if name in plan else 0))
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.num_workers = 1
    solver.solve(model)
    return {name for name, var in pick.items() if solver.value(var)}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    week = [Job("N1", "north", 30, 10), Job("N2", "north", 25, 10), Job("N3", "north", 10, 10),
            Job("S1", "south", 50, 20)]
    print(sorted(improve(week, 40, {"N3", "S1"}, {"N1", "N2", "N3"})))

cases.says: the step returns the best plan that keeps every job outside the neighborhood as it was
with nothing freed, the step returns the plan it was given
a job outside the neighborhood that the plan leaves out is not added
a job outside the neighborhood that the plan runs is not dropped

origin.section: LNS Frees Part of a Good Plan and Lets CP-SAT Rebuild It

concepts: an LNS step fixes every variable outside the neighborhood to the current plan and re-solves the rest
